haiku-low.q1: MySQL first. The change and its pending row (plus a tombstone for a delete) commit in one MySQL transaction, then the copy to Postgres runs with a 200 ms wait. If the Postgres part fails, the request still succeeds and the pending row waits for the sweeper.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming row's version is higher than the version of the row already in Postgres. Equal or lower versions change nothing. A missing row is inserted.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must show mysql_primary on app_flag_value before backfill starts. Flags are cached 30 seconds, so instances can disagree for up to about 30 seconds after a change.
haiku-low.q4: Backfill reads 2,000-row batches from the replica in id order, and pauses while replica lag is above 5 seconds. Comparer uses the same 5-second lag pause.
haiku-low.q5: Reads move only after backfill ends and a comparer pass is clean with zero confirmed mismatches, then 1, 10, 50, 100 percent, each after a clean pass. The source moves only after reads hold 100 percent for 3 days, the latest completed pass is clean, and MySQL pending is empty.
haiku-low.q6: The pending row, committed with the change in the source database's pending table, records that the other database is behind. The sweeper retries it every 10 seconds until the copy succeeds.
haiku-low.q7: A delete writes a tombstone to the target, and a copy never writes a user whose id has a tombstone there. An advisory lock on the user id stops a copy and delete of the same user interleaving.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is saved in Postgres backfill_progress, in the same transaction as each batch's rows, so a crash rolls back the open batch. The run ends when no rows remain after the last id.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer runs full passes over both tables, comparing every column including version and skipping tombstoned ids. Differences still present 60 seconds later become confirmed mismatches, and each gets a pending copy row in the current source's pending table.
haiku-low.q10: A freeze stops writes on both sides: frozen must reach every instance within 40 seconds, then switch work runs within 15 seconds, then the new mode is set. If the switch runs long, the old mode is restored. The brief does not say whether a tool enforces the limits.
haiku-low.q11: After the switch, Postgres assigns ids from its sequence, which is set above MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT. Copies into MySQL insert explicit ids, which moves its counter past them, and the rollback step checks that the counter is above every id, raising it if needed.
haiku-low.q12: MySQL stays in sync for 14 days through sweeper copies and comparer checks. Rollback sets reads to 0, freezes, drains Postgres pending, checks AUTO_INCREMENT, then sets mysql_primary. It ends at step 10, when pg_only is set and MySQL users is dropped.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: the change plus a pending row (and tombstone for delete) commit in one MySQL transaction; then, after the commit, the repository copies to Postgres (waits at most 200 ms). If the Postgres part fails or times out, the request still succeeds; the caller sees success and the pending row stays for the sweeper.
sonnet.q2: Only if the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version (the version rule). A missing row is inserted. Also, a copy never writes a user whose id has a tombstone in the target.
sonnet.q3: Every app instance must report mysql_primary (app_flag_value{flag="users.write_mode"}). Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change (flag cache is 30 s).
sonnet.q4: It reads from the replica, not the primary. It pauses (waits and rechecks) whenever replica lag is above 5 seconds (reporting jobs share the replica), and reads in batches of up to 2,000 rows in id order.
sonnet.q5: Reads: the backfill has ended and the comparer has had a clean pass (one full pass with zero confirmed mismatches); before each ramp step (1, 10, 50, 100) wait for a clean pass in comparer_runs. Source of truth: reads at 100% for 3 days, latest completed pass in comparer_runs is clean (a running pass doesn't count), and MySQL pending is empty (checked on the MySQL primary); then freeze, drain, set sequence, switch within limits.
sonnet.q6: The pending row, written in the same MySQL transaction as the change, records it. It is kept in the MySQL pending table (the database holding the source). The sweeper (every 10 s, in each worker) copies it to Postgres and deletes the pending row; the comparer also catches differences.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones and the advisory lock. Deletes write a tombstone (in the same transaction in the source, and in the target on copy), and a copy never writes a user whose id has a tombstone in the target. The advisory lock on the user id keeps a copy and a delete from interleaving. A user copied once by backfill after deletion is removed by the delete's pending row, and the tombstone blocks later copies.
sonnet.q8: In backfill_progress, in Postgres only. Each batch's rows and the saved last id are written in one Postgres transaction, so a crash rolls back the open batch and the run resumes after the last completed batch. It stops when no rows remain (no rows with id above the saved last id), after which the comparer starts.
sonnet.q9: The comparer: it runs full passes over both tables (reading the replica with the 5 s lag pause), compares every column including version, and skips tombstoned ids. Each difference is rechecked against both primaries after 60 seconds; if it remains it is a confirmed mismatch, and a pending copy row is added to the current source's pending table for the sweeper to repair. Pass results go to comparer_runs. During a freeze it checks but writes no pending rows until after.
sonnet.q10: A freeze: set write_mode to frozen, wait until the metric shows frozen on every instance (within 40 s, otherwise set the old mode back), do the switch work, set the new mode, and wait for the metric to show it on every instance. Writes during freeze get a retryable 503. If the switch work runs over 15 seconds (or drain/freeze fail), set the old mode back and try later; nothing has been switched. Total pause at most 85 s, under the 90 s limit.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids from its sequence, and the copy to MySQL keeps them. Collisions avoided at the switch by setting the Postgres sequence's next id to MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT or the sequence's current next if higher (never backwards). On rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is checked to be above every user id on either side (explicit-id copies normally move it); if not, set the counter above the highest id.
sonnet.q12: In pg_primary, writes go to Postgres first with a pending row in Postgres, and the sweeper copies to MySQL; the comparer keeps checking, for at least 14 days (step 9). Rollback: set read_from_pg to 0; freeze and wait; drain Postgres pending to zero (queried on the Postgres primary); check MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT above all ids; set write_mode to mysql_primary and wait for the metric. The option ends at step 10 (pg_only, after at least 14 days), when copies to MySQL stop and the MySQL users table is dropped; after that rollback is no longer possible.
